fact: Access Now says that from the start of the Baccalaureate on 7 June 2026 Algeria confined its exam shutdown measures to the inside of exam centres, as the Education Minister Mohamed Seghir Saadaoui explained, leaving the rest of the country connected.

Amnesty International says Algerian authorities have detained, prosecuted or convicted seven journalists and media workers since November 2025 over their work or opinions, including journalist Hassan Bouras held in pretrial detention since 12 April 2026.

Amnesty International says an Algerian court sentenced the director of the online channel Vision TV to a suspended one-year term and ordered the channel closed and its equipment seized, after journalist Saad Bouakba was convicted on 4 December 2025 over an interview given to it.

Committee for Justice reports that on 7 July 2026 the Algiers appeal court confirmed journalist Saad Bouakba's guilt for statements on historical events, reducing his sentence to 18 months suspended and a fine of one million dinars.

TSA Algerie reports that on the first baccalaureate day, 15 June 2025, social networks including Facebook and TikTok were blocked in Algeria though there was no general internet cut, and the education minister said cutting the internet is a tool to prevent exam fraud.
